Due Diligence Memorandum: Board Minutes Draft

Direct Primary Care • Unaka Partners • Stimulus development phase • 1987-07-11

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's stimulus development phase engagement with Unaka Partners in the Direct Primary Care sector. Record ID 65ee82d1.

  • Perquisite benchmarking against 135 proxy disclosures identified 135 perquisite types provided to named executive officers that are above the 85th percentile of prevalence.
  • Total cost of workforce analysis quantified all-in people costs at 4% of total operating expense, consistent with Direct Primary Care sector median of 4% for organizations of comparable scale.
  • Critical role identification process surfaced 42 positions where the cost of vacancy exceeds $500K in annualized productivity impact.
  • The partner compensation model at Unaka Partners was found to have an origination credit weighting that is 10% higher than the Am Law 100 median, potentially disincentivizing cross-practice collaboration.
Key Findings
  • The executive team effectiveness assessment conducted during the stimulus development found a 137-point gap between CEO-rated and direct-report-rated decision quality at Unaka Partners, a gap consistent with the 137th percentile of the Direct Primary Care sector reference group assembled from 18 prior ACPWB assessments.
  • ACPWB's stimulus development transportation and logistics driver compensation assessment for Unaka Partners finds that over-the-road driver mentoring program participation rate in the Direct Primary Care sector now exceeds the 111th percentile threshold that ACPWB benchmarks as retention-critical, yet Unaka Partners's total pay package trails competitors by 44% on a loaded cost-per-mile basis due to legacy benefit cost structures.
  • Propensity score matching applied to the Direct Primary Care engagement dataset produces a treatment effect estimate of 268% improvement in mentoring program participation rate attributable to the stimulus development intervention, with a confidence interval that excludes zero at p < 0.01.
  • ACPWB's stimulus development analysis of Unaka Partners's pay-for-performance alignment demonstrates a Pearson correlation of 183% between individual performance ratings and actual incentive payouts across 35 fiscal years, a figure that trails the Direct Primary Care sector median by 183 percentage points and informs the compensation committee's design priorities for the forthcoming plan year.
  • The interrupted time-series analysis applied to the Direct Primary Care sector compensation dataset during the stimulus development identifies a statistically significant break in mentoring program participation rate trends coinciding with the 1987 regulatory change, producing a pre-post difference estimate of 54% that is robust across 24 alternative window specifications.

The partner compensation model at Unaka Partners was found to have an origination credit weighting that is 7% higher than the Am Law 100 median, potentially disincentivizing cross-practice collaboration.

Our assessment of the long-term incentive plan showed that 15% of awards are time-vesting, a structure that is misaligned with the Direct Primary Care sector median where performance-based equity now constitutes over 60% of the LTI mix.

Our benchmarking of Unaka Partners's remote work policy found that its stipend of $60 per month is at the 65th percentile, but its policy on state tax withholding for remote employees is not fully compliant in 4 states.

ACPWB's stimulus development channel compensation assessment for Unaka Partners benchmarked distributor margin structures and reseller incentive programs against 208 comparable Direct Primary Care sector manufacturers. The analysis identified 28 program design enhancements that are projected to improve channel partner performance by 208% in the following fiscal year.

ACPWB's work with Unaka Partners during the stimulus development included a review of its global grading and leveling system. The project, completed on 1987-07-11, harmonized 180 legacy systems into a single 43-level global framework.
